evidence: Compared DRAFT with SOURCE.txt (the replaced words and the meaning to keep) and with its paragraph in CONTEXT, word by word. Sentence 1, “So, I came up with the idea of constructing a bridge – a temporary fix – a borrowed adulthood, if I can put it that way.”, says what his line says: he is the author (“author-developed bridge I call borrowed adulthood”, “I have developed a kind of provisional bridge”), it is a bridge, it is provisional, and its name is borrowed adulthood. “For that starting point” became “So,”, which the paragraph above anchors (people who cannot reach their adult at will; “like telling a baby bird to just fly”). “provisional” became “a temporary fix”: the same sense in this section (heading “When the adult role is not available yet”; the section already calls the situation “The problem”), and the not-proven side of “provisional” is carried by sentence 2. “if I can put it that way” is the only addition in sentence 1; it hedges his own coinage and echoes “(what I call forced adulthood)” just above; it adds no claim, condition, person or number. Sentence 2, “It’s made up of a number of familiar practices (such as modeling and supported action), even though I’m not claiming the whole sequence has been proven as one treatment.”, carries both points the change says it puts back: the practices are familiar ones, and he does not claim the whole sequence is proven as one treatment (“claiming” matches his published “without claiming”). The two named practices are the two the replaced sentence named; “such as” keeps them as examples, so witnessing and gradual transfer of responsibility from the meaning-to-keep are not denied, and the steps below show both (“Access your witnessing position”, “what you were able to do on your own (even if it’s only 5%)”). Small differences I checked and judge harmless: “but” became “even though”, which moves the caveat into a subordinate clause (a slight change of emphasis and a slightly loose concessive, but the same content and the same polarity, and it reads naturally in his casual voice); “formally tested and” is dropped, but the published line only says “validated as one treatment” and “not claiming … proven” covers it; “a number of” adds no figure. Who does what is unchanged: Joel built it and Joel is the one not claiming proof; the reader does the steps. The draft sits once in CONTEXT, between the baby-bird paragraph and “Access your witnessing position”, and reads right there. Tell rows: none found PRESENT. I looked hardest at T01 (the first person is his own authorship, from his published words), T07 (“So,” and “if I can put it that way” attach to a real thought, his own odd coinage, not to a staged beat), T15 (sentence 2 stays close to the replaced sentence because it is a put-back, and it reuses that sentence’s and his published phrases, which the inventory says is not this tell; only a connector and a couple of verbs differ), T17 and T21 (sentence 2 is a scope caveat with two jobs, his own structure, not a thesis line), and C02 (“the whole sequence” is a forward reference to the steps below, as in his source). Linter findings: B1 finished principle (flag on sentence 2) is accepted, because that sentence is his own disclaimer about the evidence status of his own method, specific to this method and mirroring his published line, so it is not a compressed aphorism; D9 follows the source order is accepted, because a two-sentence replacement of a two-sentence passage has to keep the sense-driven order of naming the thing and then stating what it is made of and its caveat, and sentence 1 notices something along the way (it flags its own coinage). One note on the writer’s reason for D9: it cites asides “of course”, “just” and “!” that are not in this draft (only “if I can put it that way” is), so that reason is partly generic, but the finding is answered anyway.
